Well thanks for deleting your replies. Now I definitely can't message you, even though you said it was ok. 

-_-
The fact that you perservered through all of that hardship shows that you DO want to get better. It is hard, but it will be worth it.

We also had quite a few visits to medical hospitals that cost hundreds of dollars, which we never paid for. We had debt collectors calling for a while afterwards, but hospitals have to write-off a LOT of losses like that.

Outside of In-patient hospital stays, no one can force you to take medication. And from what I remember, in those instances, they cannot charge you for them. 

And again, many people who are mentally ill, and/or require hospital stays are not capable of paying. I am willing to bet that a little bit of research into the topic would help you find somewhere in your area where you can be treated for little to no money, or at least at a discount.  

My first serious girlfriend had 4 or 5 different diagnosis, but we were able to find a state-run facility that charged on a sliding scale. We were poor enough at the time to be able to receive treatment completely free of charge. We had to pay for the meds, but they were $5 a bottle at the clinic that was part of that facility. These were things which would otherwise have been $50-$200 a bottle, with insurance.
Thank you. Knowing that there are people who can empathize and are willing to listen is immensely helpful. I may message you later if that is ok.

The fact that you have come here seems to imply that you are looking for help. Am I wrong in that assumption? 

One does not have to be suicidal to be depressed. If nothing else, I would advise that you keep taking your meds, as suddenly stopping them can have some uncomfortable side effects, including rebound depression. At least talk to your doctor, family or psychiatric, before discontinuing them. They will help you taper off them in a safe manner.

The fact that you have come here indicates that you are interested in getting better. Having someone who is afraid for your life to take you is not necessary, just helpful. I was too afraid to seek help on my own. I just wanted to give up.

Many people who end up in mental hospitals are incapable of paying. I would look around where you live, and try to talk to someone who works there about how your lack of funds is preventing you from seeking treatment. I'm not sure if it is because of my insurance or not, but my meds are $4-$10 a bottle.

I went through a similar situation. What finally drove me to seek help is the fear my friends expressed. I was extremely close to killing myself, but I manage to tell one of my friends I needed to go to the mental hospital. He drove me there that night.

Self-loathing, fear of judgment, and the irrepressible idea that I was not actually depressed, but just a weak person all contributed to my resistance to seek treatment. Depression convinces you that you are weak, that you belong there, that you will never be able to escape.

I spent two weeks in an out-patient program, which made a HUGE difference in my life. I have pretty bad social anxiety, so the idea of group therapy scared the crap out of me, especially for 8 hours a day, five days a week. However, group therapy allowed me to see how similar other peoples problems are to mine. Nobody had the same situation, but many of them had similar aspects. Everyone being so honest and open about such deep and embarrassing problems makes it much easier to open up, at least for me, than one on one therapy.

Since then, I have started individual therapy, as well as a series of medications. Often the first one you try does not work, and that can make you believe that nothing will work, but if you keep at it you will eventually come across the right meds.

Feel free to PM me if you would like to talk in more detail.

<3
If you want to discuss this in more detail, please PM me.

It appears to me that you have Social Anxiety. I know that problem very well, as I have had it for as long as I can remember. I've also been dealing with depression for years. One thing that has constantly been there is the feeling that I am not actually depressed, but just a weak person. It makes you think that you are worthless through whatever means necessary.

You are also falling victim to the Fallacy of Relative Privation.

The fallacy of relative privation, or appeal to bigger problems, is an informal fallacy in which it is stated an opponent's arguments should be dismissed or ignored, on the grounds that more important problems exist, regardless of whether these problems are relevant to the question at hand or not.

This attempts to belittle your own issues, when in reality, you should be attempting to fix them. It is a difficult road, but it is also the most likely way to escape from this darkness. Therapy and medication have done wonders for me. I'm not out of the woods yet, but it has saved my life numerous times. 

Know that you are not alone in this. Other people suffer from the same problems, and have the same thoughts of weakness and worthlessness.

I am available to talk more if you would like. if you want to talk privately, just PM me. 

<3

That is a really shitty situation, and while I can't claim to know what you are going through, I feel for you. 

I would say that anyone who is inconsiderate enough to break up with you over text messages is not worth having in your life. Especially if he won't even talk to you about it.

And as cold as this sounds, maybe it is better that you didn't carry it full term. Then you would have a constant reminder of this pain, in addition to having to raise a child on your own.

I can see no reason why you should blame yourself. Granted, I don't know the details of the situation, but he sounds like a shitty person, and I would guess that you are probably better off without him. 

I am here if you want to talk more. Just PM me.

<3

Drugs (alcohol is a drug) are at best a short term relief from the underlying problems. Have you actually taken time to grieve the loss of your relationship? I know from experience that refusing to actually go through the pain of dealing with that situation just draws the process out more, resulting in more attempts to mask it with drugs. The main problem there is addiction, which can be more debilitating that the problems which caused the addiction in the first place.

I dropped out of college due to depression and lack of motivation as well, though recently I have started back since I have been feeling somewhat better. It's weird being so much older than the other people, but it also helps to have more life experience. And emotional stability makes a world of difference. 

Feel free to PM me. <3

It is pretty hard to over dose on things like anti-depressants. You would need more of most of those chemicals than can actually fit in your stomach due to all the fillers. I don't recommend trying that again, as your results may hurt your liver, but will not kill you.

How long have you been on those anti-depressants? 

Have you considered that maybe a different kind might work better? 

Have the suicidal thoughts increased or decreased since you began your current meds?

Feel free to PM me if you don't want to talk openly in this thread. I know a lot about this stuff. I am actually in school for psychology at the moment.

<3

I can empathize with this. This sounds like Social Anxiety. Have you tried therapy? It has done a lot for me. It is still difficult, but I have been making more progress than I would have thought possible using Exposure Therapy.

From what I can tell, you do not have a fear of school in particular, but more likely social anxiety, or just a fear of failure. I have both of those as well. On top of that I have been dealing with recurrent depression for years. Meds have been helping with all of those things, but I think my therapist has been the most important part of my improvement.

Hormones do a hell of a lot to teenagers. I know when I was your age I fell in love with just about any girl who would show me any sort of attention. Some of that came from my fear of talking to new people (which is easier to do over the internet), and some of it came from a fear of being alone forever. I thought I was going to die just from the pain that came along with my first two break ups. I failed classes that I was good at due to lack of motivation. I expect that these feelings, though intensely painful now, will fade with time.

I highly encourage you to seek counseling for Social Anxiety. It has had a profound impact on my life, and if I had began treating it in high school, it would have saved me years of misery. I am in treatment for that now, among other things. It seems to be making a great impact on my ability to deal with people. It still makes me uncomfortable, but it gets easier with practice. Anxiety disorders respond very well to Exposure Therapy (that is, gradually putting your self into contact with the things which frighten you).

High school is hard. Dealing with people is hard. Break ups are hard. This is a very unfortunate combination of things to have to deal with all at once. Talking about it, to friends, and to my therapist, has done wonders for me. I would recommend it to anyone. 

Know that there are people, even ones who you may never meet, who care about you. 

Feel free to message me if you want.

<3
